q-221900.name: Question 1
q-221900.problem:
Select the correct options in the reasoning below.

The notation $3∣6$ means {{field-1}}. It is equivalent to the statement that there exists {{field-2}} $k$ such that {{field-3}}.
q-221900.worked_solution:
The notation $a∣b$ means $a$ divides $b.$ So, $3∣6$ means $3\text{ divides }6.$

According to the definition of integer divisibility, the fact that $a$ divides $b$ means that there exists an integer $k$ such that 

$$
b=ak.
$$

 

Therefore, $3∣6$ is equivalent to the statement that there exists $\text{an integer}$ $k$ such that $6=3k.$
